Definition: literally a cord (as an attachment); figuratively, expectancy
BiblicalUsage: Hope in this word begins as a cord — something to hold and be held by. Jeremiah says God's thoughts toward His people are thoughts of peace, to give them an expected end; the psalmist says the Lord is his hope from his youth; Proverbs says the righteous man's expectation shall not be cut off; and Hosea promises the valley of Achor for a door of hope.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hope is not wishful thinking but a cord tied to God's own promise: the expected end Jeremiah names is the reason the psalmist trusts from his youth. I believe this is the hope I am to live by — not a feeling that rises and falls, but an expectation God Himself has tied off so it cannot be cut.
